reason: You want to sit in the trade path between customer agents and order execution, and you have no SOC 2, no customers and no references. That's a non-starter at my risk committee, and frankly a proxy that checks limits and has a kill switch is something my own engineers could build on top of the controls we already run.
objection: An unaudited early-stage vendor becomes a single point of failure and a security exposure right in front of execution. If you go under or get breached, I own it with the regulator, and a free six-month pilot plus a letter of intent doesn't change that. It just puts my name on your reference list before you've earned it.
would_change_my_mind: A completed SOC 2 Type II report plus two or three named broker-dealer references running it in production. Then I'd let it through vendor review, likely in a fail-open, observe-only mode first.
